### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **607** documentable anchor(s).

**149** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76`.

⛔ **19** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`, `defaultValue (literal, 41 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`, `objectName (literal, 56 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 49 pages)`
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `45089076a39d962c144b862b39268d19d8c9e382` — the merge of head `c5fc11367642c409ba5d65656145d0624cf50ff4` into base `0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 45089076a39d962c144b862b39268d19d8c9e382 && git checkout 45089076a39d962c144b862b39268d19d8c9e382
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76 c5fc11367642c409ba5d65656145d0624cf50ff4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76 && git merge --no-ff c5fc11367642c409ba5d65656145d0624cf50ff4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b99c2b1645b101459b1dd9fd4fecdf996194a76` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a8c5d94d081c6858f792d977361b87f7564f1ff6`
Local-runs: probe — an independent byte-identity re-check: a TypeScript-parser script over `git show` output, in the scratchpad; no repo script, build, test, gate or codemod was run, and the dev's residual JSON was read the same way
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/** + scripts/codemod-split-conversions-registry.mjs (read whole), packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/shared.ts, entries/11/flow-node-http-callout-rename.ts (first), entries/18/flow-decision-mode-inclusive-explicit.ts (last), entries/15/view-visibleOn-to-visibleWhen.ts, entries/17/retry-policy-converged.ts, entries/18/page-component-filter-record-to-rule-array.ts, entries/18/declared-index-unique-scope.ts, packages/spec/scripts/conversions-major18-merge.test.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs, scripts/regen-artifacts.mjs, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__spec__src__conversions__registry.ts.json, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__spec__src__conversions__entries__18__declared-index-unique-scope.ts.json, packages/spec/export-origins/root.json, packages/spec/tsconfig.json, packages/spec/package.json (sideEffects), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, .claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md (main), .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/review-checklist.md, /mnt/project-files/issue-29987/* (report.md, dtsnorm.mjs sha256 e0b4b0c3… matches the PR body, dtsnorm-reading*.json, dtsnorm-residuals.json, codemod-dts logs, gates-ran.list), PR #29993 body, card #29987 and its 3 comments, rulings 6583399215 / 6582376616 / 6583664223 / 6591753301 / 6597555122 / 6348891160 / 6441032442, pilot PR #29598, check-runs on the head (two reads).

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: unmoved. `registry.ts` still exports exactly `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` and `ALL_CONVERSIONS` at the same path and with the same explicit types (host lines 322 and 351 are the base text); no entry module is re-exported by any entry point (every entry's own `export { NAME }` is reached only through the host import); the 3 `vi.mock('./conversions/registry', importOriginal)` tests see the same two exports. `packages/spec/export-origins/root.json` still names `src/conversions/registry.ts#ALL_CONVERSIONS` and `#CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR`, which is still true; `check:export-origins`, `check:api-surface`, `check:dual-source-exports` exit 0 in the dev's run, `Spec property liveness` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head.
- Membership and order: the whole host tail from the `OrderedConversion` docblock to EOF is byte-identical to base (my own compare, 12,413 bytes), so `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` (95 rows, sorted by identifier, every `order` value), the literal arrays for 11 (3), 15 (2) and 17 (12) and the `ALL_CONVERSIONS` flatten are unchanged; 112 host imports, one per entry, bound to 112 modules each holding exactly that `const NAME: MetadataConversion`. The `--arrays` digest proof (112/112, ALL ids sha256 6dfde603…) is consistent with this; I did not rerun it because the tables and every referenced declaration are byte-identical by construction.
- `@__PURE__`: both markers (`18: /* @__PURE__ */ inApplicationOrder(…)` and the `ALL_CONVERSIONS` flatten) are in the host, byte for byte. No entry module carries or needs one: the plan refuses any top-level expression statement, so every module holds declarations only; `packages/spec/package.json` declares `sideEffects: false`; the dev's `pure-schema-construction.test.ts` 7/7 includes the `./shared` consumer bundle.
- Ledgers: `api-surface*`, `authorable-surface*` and `export-origins` are untouched by the diff, and should be — `api-surface` is symbol-keyed (no path in it names `conversions/registry`), `authorable-surface` reads the Zod tree, and the export origin really is still `registry.ts`. `retired-after.census.*` reads `ALL_CONVERSIONS` through an import and the published `dist`, not by path: nothing to widen.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` with no changeset fits: the diff publishes nothing observable from `@objectstack/spec` — 134/134 `dist/*.d.ts` and `*.d.mts` raw byte-identical on the quiet builds, same file set, control (a renamed declaration in `action.zod-CQhac7BH.d.mts`) caught on both the normalised and surface readings; exports unchanged. That is ruling 6348891160 item 1 in its strongest form and 6441032442 item 4 (`skip-changeset` stays; no `patch` for a declaration-order diff). Precedent: pilot PR #29598 merged 2026-11-03T16:26Z with `skip-changeset`, no `.changeset/` file, its `.d.ts` passing only under the second normalisation — a weaker reading than this one. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: no (move-only)` reads as a bare `no`: `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads the arm only when the first word in the parenthetical is of the widen/narrow family, so `(move-only)` is description, not a malformed arm (PR-body guards and PM dispatch-gates green). Correct: no accept set, export or declaration moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: nothing an author can write changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (a) Irregular head builds: I read all 62 residual statements in `dtsnorm-residuals.json`. Every one is the same declaration with the property members of a `z.ZodEnum{…}` record type printed in another order (`low`/`high`, `paused`/`pending`, `critical`/`background`…); all 62 are equal after sorting lines, and the declared-surface digest is EQUAL. Two readings: (1) that class is INSIDE a declaration, so it is outside both sanctioned normalisers — 6348891160 covers only `"a" | "b"` union runs and 6441032442 B item 1(b) says a member that moves within its declaration fails (b) — and the dev's tool rightly reports `pass: false` for those builds rather than widening anything; had it been the reading of record it would be a fork on #29465, not a pass. (2) It is build noise, not a declaration difference the split causes: 4 base builds and 2 quiet head builds are raw byte-identical to each other (set sha256 757dc13d… both sides), the two irregular builds disagree with each other, both ran beside unlocked gate runs in the same worktree, and the diff class is the TypeScript printer's type-creation-order artefact that both rulings already classify as meaningless to a consumer. The cause is not established (the `--arrays` scratch copy lives under `packages/spec/.codemod-arrays-*`, but `tsconfig` includes only `src/**/*`, so that copy does not enter the program). Verdict on (a): noise; the reading of record is the quiet one. Should-fix S1 below binds Phase 1 to a quiet reading.
- (b) The 4 NOT MEASURED gates are hosted in CI on this head: `check:dts-closure` in `Type Check · debt ledger` (lint.yml:5892, success) and `Type Check · consumer gates` (lint.yml:6030, success); `check:doc-formula-expressions` in `Type Check · consumer gates` (lint.yml:6254, success); `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` in `Build Core` (ci.yml:3040 and 3064, in progress at my second read). At review time the head has 24 success, 28 in progress, 0 failure/cancelled (Build Core, Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace pending). Phase 1 regenerates anyway, so the landing CI run is the one that counts.
- (c) Skills-docs: `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` line 176 still prescribes writing the `MetadataConversion` in `conversions/registry.ts`; after the split that is a module under `entries/18/` plus one import line, and the widened merge test reds an inline definition. The dev declares the follow-up but files no card. Two more prescriptions now mis-describe the mechanics and cannot be fixed in a move-only PR: the `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` docblock (host lines 181-185, must stay byte-identical) and the `build-schemas.ts` remedy text at 1231, 2801 and 3012 (pinned by two tests). Should-fix S2.

### ④ Design judgment

- Deterministic: the script reads only the text of `registry.ts` into an in-memory ts-morph project (no node_modules, no build output, no clock); every emission is in source order or sorted; the self-test pins two runs tree-equal; the dev's two plan runs give tree sha256 960cdabf… on input 3f538689…. Re-run on a later main: `plan` refuses an input that already carries the `[#29987 codemod]` mark, so the documented `git checkout origin/main -- registry.ts` precedes `--write`; `--write` unlinks stale marked modules and refuses an unmarked file under `entries/`; a new conversion with a default/namespace import, a destructuring or an `export`ed entry exits 2 (a fork to report, never a hand edit). Sound.
- Byte identity: proof 1 compares raw `getFullText()` (leading comments and blank lines included), never normalised text, keyed by declared name, in base order per file, each base statement placed exactly once, and the undo rebuild must equal the base text. I re-implemented it independently with the TypeScript parser over `git show` output: base 159 statements, head 159 across host + 113 modules, 0 not in base, 0 missing, 0 duplicated, 0 out of order, 727,159 bytes (the dev's figure), undo tiles the base, host head (lines 1-17) identical. The `.d.ts` reading of record is raw identity; no normaliser decided anything.
- Readers by path: on main 125 files name `conversions/registry` (the dev's 110 is the scripts + packages/spec subset at 5cdaddbc); imports and prose dominate. Code readers: the 4 widened (merge test reads host imports plus each `entries/18/` module with the legacy-shape controls kept; `check-adr-0087-registration` reads `registry.ts` plus `entries/**` `.ts` via `conversionLedgerTextAt` with CR1-CR3 and the commit census widened; `affected-docs` treats host plus `entries/**` as the replay table; ADR-0120 anchor follows its entry, host keeps ADR-0087 — the entry file carries `ADR-0120` 5 times); regen-artifacts row note. Checked beyond the PR's grep: `agent-lifecycle-retirement.test.ts` and `agent-memory-store-retirement.test.ts` exclude by the prefix `packages/spec/src/conversions/`, which covers `entries/`; `check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors.mjs` names the host only in a repaired-row record; `check-future-spec-major.mjs` uses the path as a fixture label; `root-entry-migrations-split.pin.test.ts` still finds the host in the root graph. No missed path reader found.
- Import order: definition order in the host is load-bearing only for the merge test's placement rule (by design, as the definition rule was) and for nothing at runtime — each per-major array is an explicit literal or `inApplicationOrder(…)` by `order`, every module is a leaf (verify refuses a leaf importing the host or another entry; grep finds none; 98 entries import only `../shared.js`, itself a leaf), so evaluation order cannot change a table. ESLint is green on the head.
- Hand edits: none. Commits 5553ee42ec and a8c5d94d08 touch no generated file; all 114 generated files carry the mark; every statement is verbatim base text; header shapes match the generator's `wrapLineComment`.
- Note (no finding, precedent): the script's `--dts` mode carries the 6348891160 union normaliser inside `scripts/`, which that ruling's item 3 said not to do; the pilot's script did the same and merged, and the second normalisation is correctly kept out of `scripts/`.

Findings:
- S1 should-fix (Phase 1 procedure): the regenerate's `.d.ts` reading must be taken on a quiet tree (no concurrent gate run in the worktree) and the report must say so; if a quiet head build ever reproduces the record-member-order diff, it is a fork on #29465 (outside both normalisers), not a pass under either. No code change.
- S2 should-fix: file the follow-up card now and cite its number in the PR body (review-checklist: `follow-up owed` becomes `#N`), covering the SKILL.md line 176 prescription, the `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` docblock placement rule and the `build-schemas.ts` remedy text, so an agent retiring a key between landing and that fix is not sent to write a definition into `registry.ts`.
- No must-fix.
